definition: The change of an unstable nucleus, which gives out an alpha particle or a beta particle and/or gamma radiation; it happens spontaneously and at random.
A nucleus that will sooner or later change by itself and give out radiation, often because it has too many neutrons or is too heavy.
Radioactive decay in which a nucleus gives out an alpha particle (2 protons and 2 neutrons), so its nucleon number falls by 4 and its proton number falls by 2.

Radioactive decay in which a neutron in the nucleus changes into a proton and an electron, and the electron is given out as a beta particle; the nucleon number stays the same and the proton number rises by 1.
An equation in nuclide notation showing an unstable nucleus turning into a new nucleus and radiation, with the nucleon numbers and the proton numbers balanced on each side.
